discovery: The theory of hierarchical galaxy formation within cold dark matter halos

nominees.name: Simon D. M. White
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics, Garching, Germany

subfield: Cosmology and astrophysics (large-scale structure and galaxy formation)
motivation: White and Rees (1978) proposed that galaxies form when gas cools and condenses at the centres of dark matter halos that grow by hierarchical merging. This idea is the basis of all modern galaxy formation theory. Davis led the first large redshift surveys that mapped the cosmic web. He also pioneered N-body simulations of structure growth, which showed that hot (neutrino) dark matter is ruled out and that cold dark matter reproduces the observed clustering of galaxies. Together, their work turned dark matter from an anomaly in rotation curves into a predictive physical framework. That framework gave falsifiable predictions for galaxy clustering, halo structure, satellite populations and the growth of structure, and CMB, lensing and survey data have since confirmed them spectacularly. It defines our current picture of what the Universe contains and how its structure arose. It also sets the terms of today's search for the particle nature of dark matter.
